To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a Gln-134 substitution in rhodopsins induces a photoactivated helix bundle con formation around helices C (and perhaps G) in the dark state and that this is the structural basis for the hyperactivity of Glu-134 Gln rhodopsins.

(i) a Gln substitution for Glu-134 produces a photoactivated con-formation around helices F and G in the dark state and (ii) a Gln sub-stitution for Arg-135 produces a photoactivated helix bundle con-formation in the dark and light states.

the Glu-134-Gln and Arg-135-Gln mutations in rhodopsins produce a partially photoactivated conformation in the absence of light, that this conformation is localized to the helix bundle, and that the helix bundle motions accompanying activation can be uncoupled.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of G protein activation and desensitization in rhodopsins.
the structural and functional properties of rhodopsin.
the structural basis of G protein activation in rhodopsins and other G protein-couple receptors.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Glu-134 residue in rhodopsins and GPCRs has an important role in determining the helix bundle con formation and that this effect is transmitted through a network of interactions that includes the adjacent Arg-135 residue and extends to the C-terminal end of the C-helix and possibly to the G-helix.
the Glu-134/Arg-135 charge pair is a structural determinant of rhodopsin conformation in the vicinity of the cytoplasmically located C helix.
the Glu-134/Arg-135 charge pair is important in determining the conformational changes in rhodopsins and in determining the functional consequences of the changes in conformation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Glu-134/Arg-135 charge pair in helices C and E is a determinant of the helix structure in the dark state and that the Glu/Arg charge pair is a structural determinant of the activated state in the rhodopsin-G protein complex.
a single charge pair in rhodopsins can induce a significant change in structure and, therefore, function in a distant part of the molecule.
a single amino acid change at Glu- 134 can induce an activated conformation in rhodopsins in the dark state.
